set.st: Andrew Jackson of Niles hid several thousand dollars in gold after a local bank failed; a stroke took his speech and he died without telling where. His children planned to search. He died on 25 Jun 1902; a probate notice followed in July. The local paper called him perhaps the wealthiest Black resident of Berrien County; he ran a carrying business, owned several lots and had a habit of hiding his money. He was said to have tried to tell where he had buried gold coin before the stroke took his speech. His estate (Dec 1902) was about $1,600, including $800 in cash, most likely his bank deposit; no hidden gold was reported found. Pin is the street corner of his home, not the spot itself.
